# R2 to B2 occurrence-map graph projection

<!-- Generated by: Codex | Date: 2026-09-12 | Rev: 1 | Platform: Codex / win32 -->

This is a one-way, explicit projection of the migration builder's
`occurrence-content-map.jsonl` into the independent Intake filesystem graph. It
does not list/open source objects, execute or monitor transfer, write B2, classify
atomic units, select a best copy, or accept evidence.

## Wrapper

```json
{
  "schema": "intake-r2-b2-occurrence-map-v1",
  "declared_at": "2026-09-12T16:03:00Z",
  "generation_id": "caller-supplied-frozen-generation",
  "destination": "b2:salem-data/consignatio/vault/v1/",
  "occurrence_map": {
    "path": "generation/occurrence-content-map.jsonl",
    "sha256": "64-lowercase-hex"
  }
}
```

The wrapper is at most 64 KiB; its JSONL is at most 64 MiB and 10,000 rows per
projection batch. The artifact is hashed before and after parsing and the wrapper
is reread. Every row is validated before connecting to SurrealDB. Larger outputs
must be intentionally partitioned into independently hashed batches with stable
generation provenance; this adapter does not choose partitions.

Required row fields exactly follow the migration output: occurrence_id,
inventory_id, captured_at, source_bucket, source_path, size, source_md5,
content_id, identity_status, content_algorithm, content_digest,
payload_source_identity, destination_key, mapping_status, assertion_basis,
dedupe_authority, source_location_drift and is_payload_representative. Additional
fields remain preserved in the imported metadata.

## Mapping and authority

| Migration observation | Intake graph projection |
|---|---|
| Every occurrence-map row | A separate snapshot-scoped occurrence |
| source_bucket | An R2 store with root_locator `r2:<bucket>` |
| source_path | Raw and normalized object path; never reconstructed from basename |
| captured_at | Observation time from the migration inventory batch |
| Complete source row | Immutable occurrence metadata |
| Verified SHA-256 canonical/deduplicated mapping | occurrence_has_content to global raw-SHA256 content |
| MD5, unknown, held, zero-byte or drift state | Occurrence retained with no exact-content edge |
| Successful complete batch | produced_by link to completed operation, written last |

Verified SHA-256 requires mapping_status canonical/deduplicated_occurrence,
dedupe_authority sha256_verified or sha256_via_conflict_free_md5_size_bridge,
64 lowercase hex, positive size and no source-location drift. One digest with
different sizes fails before graph access. A canonical label without this exact
contract also fails. The bridge accepts the migration's finalized authority; it
does not independently make a duplicate decision.

MD5 remains metadata. Folder labels such as junk, quarantine, dupe and
to_be_deleted remain path observations. An occurrence being mapped to shared
content does not erase it, select evidentiary quality, authorize deletion, prove
an atomic-unit boundary, or merge separate exports/accounts.

The snapshot/occurrence map hash provides batch provenance. A snapshot record can
exist after partial failure; consumers require its produced_by edge to a completed
operation. Exact replay is read-only. Partial replay resumes immutable records.

## CLI

```powershell
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m casebible_index.cli graph-project-migration E:/path/wrapper.json
$env:INTAKE_SURREAL_URL='https://surreal-intake.tilapia-skilift.ts.net'
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m casebible_index.cli graph-project-migration E:/path/wrapper.json --apply
```

Validation is local. `--apply` explicitly enables graph writes but still never
executes transfer.

Completion-aware read API:

```text
GET /filesystem/graph/projections/{snapshot_key}
```

It returns the snapshot, at most one final producing-run edge, and bounded counts
for occurrences, stores, storage links and exact-content links. Consumers must
require `completion[0].status == "completed"`; snapshot existence alone is not a
success signal. The key is validated and parameter-bound. This endpoint describes
projection completion, not migration completion or corpus completeness.
